LESSON: OBSERVING AND ARTICULATING SIGNS (LISTENING AND SPEAKING) 12.1.1 LISTENING OR OBSERVING TO RESPOND: EXPRESSING FEELINGS

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.1: Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 12.1.1 Listening or Observing to Respond: Expressing Feelings
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 12.1.1 Listening or Observing to Respond: Expressing Feelings, part of Strand 12 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 9 ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: How can one express their feelings while reciting a poem? 2. Why is it important to recite or sign poems with feeling?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Observing and Articulating signs (Listening and Speaking) 12.1.1 Listening or Observing to Respond: Expressing Feelings together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to learn: the learner independently uses different words and expressions learnt to describe own feelings.

• Digital literacy: the skill of interacting with technology as the learner uses technology to search for information and record

recitations.

Values:
Unity: the learners recite and record poems emphasizing words and expressions that reveal their feelings towards the poem.

Link to other subjects:

The learner is able to relate observing skills learnt in English to their learning in Kiswahili and other learning areas.
